London, 31<sup>st</sup> March 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**The federal government** will pay for any warranty repairs on a GM or Chrysler vehicle if either company can’t because of financial problems or a bankruptcy filing, President Obama said. Obama also said he will work with Congress to try to fund credits for consumers who turn in old cars and buy cleaner, more fuelefficient automobiles.  Obama said he also will try to speed up programs to support immediate demand for auto sales. The administration will try to accelerate federal purchases of government cars and increase the flow of credit to consumers and dealers. 

_Source:  Automotive News_ 

**The U.S. task force** overseeing the restructuring of the auto industry said the plans submitted by GM and Chrysler failed to show how they could be viable.  A new car czar, Edward Montgomery, will oversee the turnaround.  Under the current plan, conclusions were that GM’s plan would not provide viability over the long term even if the economy improved.  Chrysler too would not be viable over the long term as a stand-alone company, and its plan contained a number of “unrealistic or overly optimistic” assumptions. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**Ford,** the only U.S. automaker not taking federal aid, could lose its competitive edge if President  Obama is successful in slimming down GM with lower labor costs, debt and dealers.   Obama gave GM 60 days to come up with a new strategy to cut costs with its union, slash debt with bondholders and reduce dealers and brands. If GM does all that, it may have significantly lower costs than Ford, said auto analyst John Wolkonowicz of IHS Global Insight.  Ford is prepared to do whatever is necessary to remain competitive, including going beyond the cost-cutting efforts already under way, spokesman Mark Truby said.  Ford will offer buyouts valued at as much as $75,000 to all 42,000 of its U.S. hourly workers. _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**FNX Mining** is prepared to act quickly to reduce, increase or suspend production as conditions warrant, but would wait for proof of a sustained recovery in metal prices before restarting halted operations, said CFO Ron Gagel.  At end-08, it had an unaudited cash balance of C$129,6-millionand no debt.  FNX has an agreement with Gold Wheaton, which buys 50% of the precious metals produced at Sudbury.  FNX posted net loss of C$397,4-million in Q408, compared with profit of  C$32,28-million in Q407. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**Braemore Resources** is accelerating its move into refining the platinum it produces from its ConRoast plant to bolster operating margins in a difficult market.  Braemore is licensed by Mintek to use the ConRoast technology that can cope with high levels of chrome in platinum group metals concentrate, a particular problem widely used smelting technology cannot overcome.  Braemore posted a deeper interim loss of £4.4m for the period to end-December 2008 from £1m the year before. This was largely du

e to the settlement of an old contract at a cost of £2m. In all, Braemore produced 6,892 oz of PGMs during the period, securing recoveries of 99.52%. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**AU Optronics (AUO) and Chi Mei Optoelectronics (CMO)** have placed equipment orders to expand their 6G LCD panel capacity amid increasing utilization rates driven by the consumer electronics promotion program in China, according to industry sources.  The equipment orders were placed to meet continued orders for LCD TV panels in the 22- to 28-inch segments from China. AUO and CMO may see their 6G production lines reach full capacity in the second quarter. AUO’s current 6G production utilization rates are estimated to be 80-90%.  Innolux Display has delayed equipment installation at its 6G plant to 2010, but it may start install some of the equipment in the third or fourth quarter this year, the sources said. _Source: Digitimes_
